item.title: Thoracic HVLA — Clinical Setup & Safety Principles
clinicalUse: Selected thoracic mechanical pain/hypomobility when trained clinician judges a thrust appropriate
patientPosition: Position depends on the trained technique; patient must be comfortable and consented.
therapistPosition: Only clinicians with supervised practical HVLA training should perform the thrust component.
stabilization: Control adjacent segments and avoid excessive end-range preloading.
contact: Region-specific contacts are taught hands-on; avoid learning thrust contact from text alone.
forceDirection: A short low-amplitude thrust is delivered through a controlled setup; cavitation is not the target.
dosage: Usually one carefully selected attempt or a very small number; do not repeat forcefully to chase a click.
steps: 1. Confirm indication and exclude fracture/instability/systemic risk.
2. Explain benefits, alternatives and risks; obtain consent.
3. Establish comfortable setup with minimal pre-thrust tension.
6. Immediately re-check pain, motion and neurological status.
mistakes: Using HVLA when mobilization/exercise would be equally suitable.
safety: Not appropriate as a text-only self-teaching procedure; formal practical training, consent and screening are required.
item.visualCue: Screen + consent → controlled setup → brief trained thrust → immediate re-test.

subTechniques.name: Thoracic HVLA Safety Framework
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Guide clinical selection, consent and reassessment without teaching a thrust maneuver from text
subTechniques.patientSetup: Prone, side-lying or supported sitting according to target.
subTechniques.contact: Region-specific contact over Selected thoracic region using the parent technique principles.
subTechniques.direction: Region-specific thrust direction is taught only in supervised practical training
subTechniques.dosage: Use a conservative response-guided trial and reassess before repeating.
subTechniques.reassess: Thoracic ROM, pain and neurological status
subTechniques.safetyNote: Do not learn or perform HVLA from text-only instructions; formal hands-on training and screening are required.
